definitions.purpose: Acceptance check: beat, claim and VisualTask are never conflated. These definitions are taken from the schema, the two builders and the Matching splitter, not from intuition.

beat.schema: storypackage-0.2.schema.json#/properties/beats/items: required beatId (opaque, unique within storyId), order, span (code points into script.text), narration, claimIds, claimCoverage; optional section, test, story{beatRole,retentionFunction}, speaker{role,entity,label,sourceTimestamp,source,provenance}. No field defines what a beat means semantically.
beat.taggedBuilder: tools/build_tagged_script.py lines 82-105: one `@role [slug] [HH:MM:SS]` tag line plus exactly one paragraph (no internal newline) is one beat; ids p<part>-<n>. Used for future-volksgeist and jayz-drake-settle-it.
beat.yearSeventeenBuilder: tools/build_year_seventeen.py lines 22-43: every blank-line-separated block under a `###` section heading that is not a heading, test question or `---` is one beat; ids c<cycle>-<section>-<n>; carries `test` (the cycle's test question).
beat.sourceTranscript: youtube_doc_analysis/transcripts/full/*.txt: 30-second caption chunks with no punctuation and no speaker turns (cleaning log). No beat concept.
beat.sourceAnalysis: youtube_doc_analysis/analyses/analysis_006.json and analysis_002.json `story_beats[]`: act-level narrative beats B1..B18 (60–360 s each) with beat_role, retention_function, devices. 18 for the Future source, 15 for the ranking-debate source.
beat.legacyReviewBeat: grammar/beat-review-export-2026-09-27.json `beats[]`: 40 review beats keyed NN-NN[a-z] with a `quote` in older narration wording; joined to Story claims through claims[].reviewKeys.
beat.editorUsage: In candidate_acceptability evidence the editor writes 'beat' for the Matching-derived task proposal (for example ev_0c2a0aba000bca29 'beat should be split into 2' on taskId ...matching-derived-p05-2-03).
beat.consistency: Not consistent. Five distinct units share the word. The schema permits this (beatId is opaque) but the Matching splitter treats the Story beat as the hard outer boundary of every derived VisualTask (pipeline/storypackage_splitter.py `_semantic_units`, called per beat at lines 456-489), so paragraphing conventions govern downstream granularity.

claim.schema: storypackage-0.2.schema.json#/properties/claims/items: the semantic/evidentiary unit; required claimId, beatId, span, text (must equal script.text at span), lane (factual|interpretive|editorial), entityRefs[{entity,mentioned,display,representedBy}], provenance; optional branchId, phrasing, status, receipts, editorPriority, cohortRefs, values, reviewKeys, unresolvedMentions. SPEC-0.2 'Boundary': a package never makes one claim equal one VisualTask.
claim.taggedBuilder: build_tagged_script.py line 83 SENT regex: split after . ? ! (optionally followed by a closing quote) then whitespace then a non-lowercase character; line 101 never splits inside an open double quotation. One sentence = one claim; ids <beatId>.<n>.
claim.yearSeventeenBuilder: build_year_seventeen.py line 39: split after . ? ! then whitespace, except after 'J.'. One sentence = one claim.
claim.operationalMeaning: A claim is a sentence of the exact script with a lane and entity roles. It is an evidentiary span, not a visual unit.

visualTask.storySide: Deliberately absent from storypackage-0.2 (schema description; SPEC-0.2 'StoryPackage never ... makes one claim equal one VisualTask'). jobProposals[] are advice only (claimIds, optional sub-span, job from a 20-value enum, provenance). matching-handoff-0.2 tasks[] (year-seventeen only) carry story-owned presentation requirements per VisualTask id after Matching has named the tasks.
visualTask.matchingSide: pipeline/storypackage_splitter.py `task_from_claims` (lines 270-353): a review-only taskProposal with claimIds, claimSpans, proposalSpan, taskText, lanes, entityRefs, cohortRefs, values, obligations and continuity attached by claim intersection, presentationOperations, primaryPresentationOperation, routeDisposition, activationState 'proposal_requires_editor_review'. Produced (i) by materializing a Story proposal (lines 355-388), (ii) per quote beat (lines 396-412), or (iii) per narrator beat by `_semantic_units` (lines 456-489). Clip beats become speakerRoutes with templateMatchingEligible false, not tasks.
visualTask.operationalMeaning: A VisualTask proposal is the Matching layer's unit of template/media admission: an exact source span plus everything attached to its claims. It is derived from, and may cut across or merge, claims; it never crosses a Story beat unless a Story proposal does.

definitions.jobProposal: storypackage-0.2 jobProposals[]: {proposalId, claimIds (1+), span (optional sub-span inside one claim), job (enum of 20 legacy matcher jobs), provenance}. Advice; a proposal never becomes a VisualTask without review.
definitions.obligation: storypackage-0.2 obligations[]: {obligationId, claimIds, intent, mustBeTrue, mustBePerceptible, wouldBeALie, withheld, mediaNeeds[{kind,count,constraints}], recognizableIdentityCount, needsOnScreenText, contentClass, provenance}. Task inputs, not template assignments.
definitions.continuity: storypackage-0.2 continuity[]: {groupId, claimIds (2+), scope (template|template_family|visual_grammar|palette|sequence|subject_framing|adjacency), invariant, strength (required|preferred), provenance}.
definitions.visualMoment: Analytical term used in this report only: the smallest span of narration that one continuous on-screen treatment must communicate. Neither schema has it as a first-class object. The handoff's media.focal {simultaneous, sequencePermitted, storyItems} and the splitter's semantic unit are the nearest approximations.

findings.title: Five incompatible meanings of 'beat', and the Story paragraph is the one Matching treats as a wall
findings.statement: Source caption chunks, source-analysis narrative beats (15–18 per documentary, minutes long), legacy review beats (40, older wording), Story beats (paragraphs: 94 / 54 / 72) and the editor's 'beat' (a Matching task proposal) are five different units. The schema makes beatId opaque, so Story is within contract. But the splitter derives semantic units per Story beat and never crosses one (except through a Story proposal that does), so paragraph conventions set the ceiling of every VisualTask. Narrator paragraphs are 4.6× longer in one story than another (median 662 vs 143 code points).
findings.storyShare: Paragraphing is authored at cleaning or writing time with no stated visual rule; the largest beats hold 12–16 sentences.
findings.matchingShare: Beat as hard outer boundary; no cross-beat moment unless Story proposes it.
findings.wouldSettle: n/a (observed in code: storypackage_splitter.py lines 456-489; build_tagged_script.py lines 85-105; build_year_seventeen.py lines 26-42)

findings.title: Claim equals sentence; a sentence is neither the visual moment nor a reliable fraction of one
findings.statement: Both builders cut claims at sentence punctuation. The spans show sentences holding two or three moments (S05, S06-adjacent, S16, S17, S19, S22) and moments spanning several sentences (S10, S11, S15). The contract already says a claim is not a VisualTask (SPEC-0.2 'Boundary'; MATCHING_LAYER_FEEDBACK.md §1). What is missing on both sides is a first-class moment boundary: Story's proposals can carry sub-spans and multi-claim groups but the general builder authors neither (0 sub-spans in two packages, 1 in the third); Matching's intra-claim split has one hard-coded pattern and its merge rule keys on shared entity and a 260-code-point cap.
findings.storyShare: Sub-span and cross-claim proposals are schema-legal but builder-unsupported in general form.
findings.matchingShare: Moment discovery is heuristic keyword matching over text (storypackage_splitter.py lines 34-110, 162-248).

findings.title: Obligations and continuity are valid boundary evidence that Matching attaches after the fact and never uses to group
findings.statement: Every obligation and continuity group carries a claimIds set that names which sentences belong to one treatment. `_semantic_units` receives only beat, claim ids and claims; obligations and continuity are joined to a finished task by intersection (lines 334-339). In S10 the obligation's set is exactly the two moments the editor asked for; in S12 and S15 the obligation or continuity names the pair the splitter broke.

findings.title: Lanes are never consumed by Matching
findings.statement: The lane heuristics (questions and first person → editorial; hedges → interpretive; clip/quote → factual attribution) produce usable labels: 116 of 222 claims editorial in the debate story, 107 of 502 in the biography. The splitter copies lane into the task and never conditions an operation or job on it, so editorial sentences containing number words are derived as data_explanation and receive counters (S13).
findings.storyShare: Lanes are heuristic plus hand correction, all story_writer proposed, none user-reviewed (handover documents). Precision is adequate in the sampled spans.

findings.title: Participants are counted from entityRefs alone; values' entities and the implied comparison partner are invisible
findings.statement: Comparison and parallel derivation require two or more display-eligible entityRefs. In S12 the values already name both entities; in S04 the obligation names the partner; in both the sentence names one. The Story implied-reference tables (DRAKE_CUES/FORCE_DRAKE in build_year_seventeen.py; impliedRefs in the story configs) cover pronoun cues but not comparison partners. The merge key for adjacent claims is shared entity, so head-to-head pairs that alternate entity are split while same-entity different-metric sentences are merged (S11).
findings.storyShare: implied-partner refs missing on comparison sentences
findings.matchingShare: values[].entity and values[].label unused for participant and metric identity

findings.title: jobProposals: advisory, incomplete, and carrying the legacy matcher vocabulary
findings.statement: Two packages propose only pose_a_question (20 and 14), which the splitter derives anyway from '?', so the proposals add nothing. The third proposes 116: 36 are legacy model labels from the review export, 72 story_writer, 8 user; 32 are assert_without_data (the null job). The job enum is the legacy matcher's 20 jobs (HANDOFF_data_matching_media.md §0 says claim types 'deliberately mirror the matcher's communication jobs'). Proposals carry boundaries that disagree with obligations (S06, S08) and overlap each other (S02). The Year Seventeen gold reference is a one-to-one materialization of these proposals, so its 'visual job derivation' is the Story's labels; the current splitter demotes 12 of them to advisory and re-derives their units (job preserved). Where proposals are user-approved with a ruling (S07) they are precise and valuable.
findings.storyShare: all for content; the enum choice is a contract decision shared with Matching
findings.matchingShare: over-materialization of every proposal on a multi-proposal claim yields overlapping tasks (S02)

findings.title: Obligations are structurally precise where authored and empty where the editor's note was only quoted
findings.statement: mustBeTrue is used by 0 of 72 obligations across the three packages; contentClass by 0. Six Year Seventeen obligations (o-13-13b, o-14-14, o-21-21b, o-23-23, o-25-25a, o-29-29a) carry no field other than claimIds and a provenance.evidence string that quotes the review note. Counts are often prose ('multiple rappers from the pre-streaming era', 'for the first sentence') where the schema offers mediaNeeds.count, recognizableIdentityCount, or a cohort with members_not_enumerated and expectedCount. Quoted text inside narrator sentences gets no needsOnScreenText (S20). There is no narration disposition for lines the production will replace (S18). Where fields are used (S01, S03, S10, S21, the debate story's six) they are exact and user-provenanced.

findings.title: The entity model covers people and groups only; works and unenumerated groups cannot be expressed
findings.statement: 'These mixtapes', 'all of his interviews', 'an entire generation of music artists', 'the Jet Life run', '13 album covers' are visual subjects that are not registry entities. The biography package has 0 cohorts and 0 values; its only structural handles are person refs. The editor's recurring instruction that 'things in multiples' need multi-item treatments has no Story signal to key on. The registry is Data-owned (shared roster v12), so widening it is not Story's alone; but the schema's cohort (members_not_enumerated, expectedCount) and mediaNeeds.count fields exist today and were unused for these spans.
findings.wouldSettle: Owner decision on whether works become registry entities (Data) or stay obligation-level media needs (Story).

findings.title: Beat and claim derivation is unverifiable against sources, and Year Seventeen review evidence was written against different wording
findings.statement: No transcript-to-beat mapping exists (Job 1). For the biography, every sentence and paragraph boundary was created during caption cleaning. For the debate story the script is original. For Year Seventeen, 21 of the 40 legacy review beats quote narration that differs from script v2.1 (overlap down to 0.632), and the beat-script map the builder used to join them (grammar/beat-script-map.json) is absent from this checkout. Editor notes cited through reviewKeys therefore attach to re-worded sentences. This does not invalidate the notes; it bounds how exactly a note can be re-applied to a span.

findings.title: Matching granularity drifted between the gold runs and the baseline on unchanged Story input
findings.statement: Year Seventeen: gold materializes all 116 proposals; baseline materializes 104 and re-derives 11 units (one merge). Biography: claim structure is byte-identical between package files @3 and @5, yet 2 beats are grouped differently and 26 tasks change job label; counts are equal (310). This is not a Story failure. Whether the baseline is better or worse than the gold on these units is a Job 4 judgment; this job records that equal counts conceal the change.
findings.wouldSettle: The splitter revision that produced each gold file.

findings.title: The three packages are not produced the same way and do not carry the same structure
findings.statement: Two builders (tagged, Year Seventeen-specific) with different sentence regexes and beat conventions; values in one package only (62), cohorts 0/1/3, reviewKeys in one, receipts in one, a matching handoff for one (hand-authored per task in build_matching_handoff.py, keyed to Matching's pilot task ids, not a general producer). UE-03 is therefore a sequencing dependency: the two newer handovers ask Matching to return VisualTasks first so Story can write the handoff. Fitness of this contract is Job 3's question.

findings.title: Speaker roles (clip, quote) are a success end to end
findings.statement: The Story expresses who is heard per beat with provenance for uncertain attributions; clip beats carry footage obligations and quote beats carry on-screen-text obligations; Matching routes clips out of template matching and quotes to an attributed-quote task, and emits typed gaps (36 clip end-timing, 6 unidentified speakers, 1 missing quote source). The editor's expectation that narration hand-offs resolve into the following clip is met by the Story structure.

principles.principle: A visual moment is the unit of treatment; a claim is the unit of evidence; a beat is the unit of narration. Each layer must carry its own unit and name the mapping between them explicitly.
principles.derivedFrom: S02, S05, S10, S17; SPEC-0.2 Boundary; MATCHING_LAYER_FEEDBACK §1
principles.referenceSupport: Year Seventeen handoff tasks link claims, sub-spans and focal counts (Story-authored); the Future gold reference's granularityPolicy states 'claimBoundaryIsEvidenceNotTaskBoundary' (Future reference only; the Year Seventeen reference has no such field).

principles.principle: Any Story object that enumerates a claim set for one purpose (obligation, continuity, proposal) is boundary evidence and must be consulted before text heuristics decide a moment's edges.
principles.referenceSupport: Year Seventeen reference: tasks for user split proposals (28-28) follow the claim sets the user named.

principles.principle: Participants in a comparison are the union of mentioned entities, implied entities, value entities and cohort members, never the mentioned set alone; the merge key for adjacent sentences is shared metric or shared moment, not shared entity.
principles.referenceSupport: Neither reference demonstrates this; it is derived from editor evidence and Story value labels.

principles.principle: Every number, rank, count and threshold spoken in narration should exist as a structured value with entity, basis and label, in every package, so that data-aware derivation behaves the same across stories.
principles.referenceSupport: The debate package's values; the Year Seventeen handoff's anchored values (Story-authored).

principles.principle: Groups the narration treats as a visual multiple (people, works, events) need a typed count even when membership is unknown; prose constraints are not machine-usable.
principles.referenceSupport: Year Seventeen handoff focal counts and the typed 'focal_unknown' item for the pre-streaming group.

principles.principle: Lane is a routing signal: editorial and interpretive sentences default to text, question or b-roll treatments unless an obligation says otherwise.
principles.referenceSupport: Not shown by either reference; derived from editor evidence.

principles.principle: Narration the production will replace or omit must be marked as such in the package, not inferred from an obligation's intent string.
Job labels are advisory operations; moment boundaries and requirements are the binding advice. A proposal with a user ruling outranks a legacy label.
principles.referenceSupport: Year Seventeen reference: the 8 user proposals are the most precise units in it; 32 of its 116 jobs are the null job.

principles.principle: Evidence written against one wording of a sentence is scoped to that wording; a re-worded sentence needs the note re-affirmed before it binds.
principles.referenceSupport: Timing boundary ev_0ef11e34ab9fe948 quotes older wording.

recommendations.what: Add a first-class moment boundary: generalize jobProposals (or a new `moments[]`) to carry exact spans across one or more claims, optional job, and provenance; make both builders accept an authored moment table so sub-spans are not hand-coded one at a time.

Consume obligations.claimIds, continuity.claimIds, values.label/entity and lane as grouping evidence before keyword heuristics; never split a claim set an obligation names unless a Story proposal does.

Emit values for every spoken number in every package; emit cohorts with members_not_enumerated and expectedCount for unenumerated groups; emit mediaNeeds.count for works in multiples; emit needsOnScreenText for quoted text inside narrator claims.
Replace obligation shells with fields: move each quoted review note into intent, mustBePerceptible, mediaNeeds or a proposal boundary; keep the quote in provenance.evidence.
Add a narration disposition (render, replace, omit) at claim or beat level, with provenance.
Record the script wording hash each review note was written against; re-affirm notes on re-worded sentences before they bind through reviewKeys.
Report grouping and job-label diffs between runs on identical Story input, not only counts.
